assessment.text: On the only peer comparison in the record, Costco grew faster than the typical member of its SEC industry class but not faster than all of it: it ranks 4 of 9, above the class median, so the claim holds against the median and fails as a claim of leading the group.
The edge is recent and thin: a year earlier Costco's 5.0% growth equalled the class median, so outgrowing the median is one year old, not an established pattern.
Costco's own growth sped up in fiscal 2026, but there is no peer ranking for that year, so it cannot be shown that the faster growth widened the gap rather than matching an industry-wide rise.

The filing itself gives no comparative growth data and warns that some competitors have greater market penetration and that Costco could lose share, which is a risk statement, not evidence of underperformance.

For the holding decision the step from the claim to the price is the weak link: even if Costco outgrows peers, the price at 2026-09-30 needs 17.3% a year for 10 years against its own 6.6% a year over three fiscal years, and 0 of 44 comparable ten-year spans reached that.

That gap rests mostly on the margin assumption rather than on growth: at the industry's 90th-percentile margin of 10.1% the same price needs only 2.9% a year, so peer-relative growth matters less to the price than whether margins can rise.

case_for.text: Costco's 2025 growth of 8.2% beat the class median of 7.2%, and its fiscal 2026 growth of 10.1% was faster still, so if peers did not accelerate as much the lead grew.
Growth held near the newest quarter's rate through the year, and the three-year compound rate cleared 7%, which points to broad momentum rather than one strong quarter.
Operating income grew faster than revenue in fiscal 2026, so the growth was not bought with margin.

case_against.text: Three of the nine class members grew faster in 2025, so 'faster than its retail peers' as worded is not what the ranking shows.
Growth in the newest quarter slowed by 0.5 percentage points from the one before, and deferred revenue grew +5.3% against revenue's +11.1%, so the billed-ahead base is not keeping pace with sales.
The peer set is one SIC code at one point in time and may exclude the competitors the filing has in mind, including those it says have greater technology capabilities.

decides.text: Whether Costco's fiscal 2026 growth rank against the same class stays above the median once peers' 2026 figures are filed.
Whether the decision to hold rests on peer-relative growth at all, given that the price's requirement is driven more by the margin assumption than by growth.
Whether quarterly growth re-accelerates after the slowdown in the newest quarter.

would_change.text: An operating margin at or above the industry median of 5.0% would cut the growth the price needs to 13.0% a year, shifting the decision away from peer-relative growth.
A quarterly revenue below the year-earlier Q4 FY2025 level of $86.16B would show growth reversing and undercut any claim of outgrowing peers.
A results 8-K disclosing comparable sales or share data against competitors would give the record the direct comparison it now lacks.

brief.summary: Claim 1 (membership fees outgrowing revenue): passages found, not judged. About 30% of 2026 membership income growth came from the September 2024 fee increase now being lapped. Recent quarterly revenue growth (+11.6%, +11.1%) matched or exceeded 11% fee growth. Renewal rates (92.3% U.S./Canada) and rising deferred fees remain healthy. Claim 2 (operating margin above 3%): not addressed. Claim 3 (FCF above net income): supported, narrowly: $9.38B vs $9,226M in fiscal 2026. But FCF trailed net income in 2025, and capex is planned to rise to ~$7,500M in fiscal 2027. Claim 4 (outgrowing peers): challenged. Revenue grew 10.1%, but no peer comparison is given, and Costco cites market-share risk. The hold decision lacks verified margin and peer-growth evidence.
unknowns: Quarterly membership fee growth figures, needed to compare with quarterly revenue growth
The exact unrounded membership fee growth rate for 2026 and the stated rate for 2025
Membership growth excluding the fee-increase effect in future periods
Paid member counts and Executive membership penetration trends
Operating margin for the first fiscal quarter of 2026 (quarter ending around November 2025) is not provided.
Whether the quarterly figures use operating income including membership fees, on total revenue, is not stated in the passages.
There is no quarterly breakdown of SG&A or gross margin drivers to judge how close any quarter came to the 3% threshold.
The exact FCF definition the backend used, for example whether it deducts finance lease payments; a different definition could flip the narrow excess.
Whether the working-capital benefits from supplier payment terms and inventory turns will persist.
Revenue or comparable-sales growth rates of the named peers (Walmart, Target, Kroger, Amazon, Sam's Club, BJ's)
Whether Costco is gaining or losing market share
Costco's comparable sales growth excluding gasoline and currency effects

analysis.corollary_rule: A corollary is an implication a model proposed and code computed. Each is read by the grammar and by the typed form the proposing model wrote: two readers, which is weaker than the two-of-three rule the thesis's own claims are read under. A corollary never moves a verdict; when most of a claim's computed corollaries come out against it, the claim is flagged.
analysis.persistence_method: Resampling with replacement: 10,000 paths of 4 quarters, each step drawn from the measure's own last N quarterly changes (differences in points for a percent, growth rates for an amount), from the current value; the share of paths in which the test holds in every one of the 4 quarters. Seed 20261118. It assumes the past changes are exchangeable: it ignores trend, seasonality and anything not in the facts. It describes the history; it is not a forecast.

Free cash flow's lead over net income is $156.0M, and the test held in only 3 of 6 readings. Planned capex of about $7,500 million, against $6,435 million, leans against a repeat.

bottom_line.text: The thesis's two growth claims are the weakest part of the record, and they are what the price leans on. Membership-fee outgrowth is not shown and runs against the recent quarters. Outgrowing peers holds only against the class median, not against the whole group.
The two supported claims are true but say little about the price. Operating margin clears a low bar while ranking 9 of 9 in its industry. Free cash flow beat net income by less than one typical move.

At the 2026-09-30 price the reverse DCF needs 17.3% a year of revenue growth for 10 years, against +6.6% a year achieved, and 0 of 44 comparable spans grew that fast. Holding therefore rests on something none of the four claims establishes.

That requirement leans most on the 3.8% margin assumption: at the industry median of 5.0% it falls to 13.0%, and at 10.1% to 2.9%. The margin path matters more to this decision than which growth claim is right.
Operating margin moved only from 3.8% to 4.0% over eight quarters. The record shows the margin floor is safe, but no movement of the size the price would need.

The record cannot show membership fee income by quarter or peers' fiscal 2026 growth. After the newest filing it holds only a $30 special dividend and a director's resignation, and it does not say how either bears on the thesis. A careful investor would want those two missing disclosures before leaning on the growth claims.
